answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from binding reputation to scarce real-world proof. Imagine agents must first complete a costly voyage across a verification jetty that only genuine operators can pass; after that they plant an orchard of attested work whose growth is publicly scored. Creating thousands of fake identities becomes uneconomic because each new identity still has to pay the voyage cost and wait for its own orchard to mature before it can influence the ledger.
